task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the median length of a trapezium.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method MedianLength(a: real, b: real, c: real, d: real) returns (median: real)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The median length is correctly calculated based on the four side lengths of the trapezium
- The returned median is the middle value when the four side lengths are sorted in non-decreasing order
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method MedianTrapeziumLength(a: int, b: int, c: int, d: int) returns (median: int)

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The input lengths can be any integers; no specific preconditions are necessary.

Dafny specification:
    // No preconditions required; lengths can be any integers.

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The median length is the middle value among the four input lengths when sorted
- The median is greater than or equal to the smallest input length
- The median is less than or equal to the largest input length

Dafny specification:
    ensures median == (sorted(a, b, c, d))[1]  // second element in sorted order
    ensures exists sortedList :: sortedList == sort([a, b, c, d]) && median == sortedList[1]

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method MedianTrapeziumLength(a: int, b: int, c: int, d: int) returns (median: int)
    ensures exists sortedList :: sortedList == sort([a, b, c, d]) && median == sortedList[1]
{
    var lst := [a, b, c, d];
    var sortedList := sort(lst);
    median := sortedList[1]; // second element in sorted list (middle for even count)
}
```
